security.title: Security
security.intro: Hardening options. The defaults are the secure choice; change one only when your deployment needs it.
security.sessionMaxAgeHint: A login ends after this long even when it is in use (1–720; default 168 = 7 days). Active Directory, Kerberos and Microsoft sign-in sessions end after 12 hours at the latest.

security.frameAncestors: Sites that may embed NetworkMonitor in a frame

telegram.help2: Private chat: open your bot and press Start. Group: add the bot to the group and send a message there. Channel: add the bot as an administrator.
telegram.help3: Then open the following address in a browser and copy the number after <c>"id"</c> in the <c>"chat"</c> section:
telegram.help4: Group and channel IDs are negative (supergroups start with <c>-100</c>). For a public channel you can also use <c>@channelname</c>.

escalation.title: Escalation and reminders
escalation.help: Escalation sends the problem to more channels when it is neither acknowledged nor recovered after the given time (measured from when the problem began). Reminders repeat the notification to the rule channels. Both stop when the problem is acknowledged, recovers, or the device is in maintenance.
escalation.afterHint: From the start of the problem; at least the delay above (1 minute to 7 days).

escalation.repeatHint: Sent to the rule channels; 5 minutes to 7 days.

features.title: Features
features.intro: Every feature of this release is off by default. Turning one on or off takes effect immediately, without a restart; stored data is kept while a feature is off. Features with a settings tab of their own are switched in that tab.
features.askAdmin: Ask an administrator to turn it on.

name.ai_template_drafts: Template drafts from an SNMP walk

desc.traps: Receive SNMP traps (v1/v2c/v3) from devices, store and search them.
desc.syslog: Receive syslog messages (UDP and TCP), store and search them.
desc.event_alerts: Turn traps and syslog messages into alerts through event rules (event sensors per device).
desc.lag: Show link aggregation (LAG/trunk) membership in the ports view.
desc.ldap: Let Active Directory users sign in with their domain account (local accounts keep working).
desc.audit: Record who changed what, and every login, in a tamper-proof audit log.
desc.timeline: A per-device timeline of status changes, notifications, traps, syslog and changes.
desc.flapping: Detect ports that go up and down repeatedly and hold back their link alerts.
desc.siem_forwarding: Forward received traps and syslog to a SIEM (RFC 5424 over UDP, TCP or TLS).
desc.config_backup: Collect switch and router configurations over SSH (read-only), keep versions, show diffs and alert on changes.
desc.flows: Receive NetFlow v5/v9, IPFIX and sFlow and show top talkers, applications and interface traffic.
desc.new_device_alerts: Alert when a never-seen device (MAC address) appears on an access port.
desc.sso_kerberos: Domain PCs sign in automatically with their Windows account.
desc.sso_oidc: A "Sign in with Microsoft" button (Entra ID, with MFA).
desc.reports: Weekly or monthly reports by email or channel: availability, alerts, ports, changes.
desc.noc: Full-screen status pages for wall screens, opened with a secret link from allowed addresses only.
desc.chat_ack: An "Acknowledge" button in Telegram, and a link in Teams and email messages.
desc.assistant: Connection to Amazon Bedrock and the "Ask the network" page for administrators. Master switch of every AI feature.
desc.ai_explain_alert: An "Explain" button on problems, events and sensors: what happened, what preceded it, likely cause and next checks.
desc.ai_correlation: Groups related problems (dependencies, topology, same device) into incidents with a short AI summary.
desc.ai_alert_notes: Adds a 1–2 line AI note after the first problem notification of rules that opt in. Never delays the alert.
desc.ai_config_diff: Risk flags and a plain-language explanation on configuration diffs.
desc.ai_syslog_digest: Every morning: what was unusual in yesterday's syslog compared to the previous week.
desc.ai_rule_drafts: "Describe the rule…" in the alert-rule and event-rule forms fills the form with a draft for review.
desc.ai_template_drafts: Bounded read-only SNMP walk of a device and a device-template YAML draft for review.
desc.ai_knowledge: Lets the assistant search your Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base (runbooks, diagrams) and cite it.
desc.ai_chat_ask: Linked administrators can send /ask <question> to the Telegram bot in a private chat.
desc.ai_report_summary: A short narrative paragraph at the top of reports that opt in.

hint.needsIngest: Needs SNMP traps or Syslog to be on to receive anything.

hint.flappingTraps: Uses linkUp/linkDown traps when SNMP traps are on, plus interface sensors and the port inventory.
hint.ldapConfig: Complete the Active Directory settings first (service account, password, servers or domain, a group).
hint.timelineSources: Traps, syslog and audit entries appear when those features are on.
hint.lagPorts: Uses the port inventory (devices with ports enabled).
hint.sshCredentials: Needs SSH credentials on the devices or their groups.
hint.backupSyslog: Backups triggered by configuration-change messages need Syslog.
hint.flowExporters: Configure flow export on the switches/routers to this server (UDP 2055, 4739 or 6343).
hint.newdevFdb: Uses the port inventory (MAC tables) of the switches.
hint.kerberosLdap: Needs Active Directory login turned on and configured (roles come from the AD groups).
hint.keytab: Needs a keytab uploaded under Settings → Single sign-on.
hint.oidcSetup: Needs an Entra ID app registration and outbound HTTPS through the proxy.
hint.reportsDelivery: Scheduled sends need SMTP or a Teams/Telegram channel.
hint.publicUrl: The Teams/email link needs the public URL (Settings → General).
hint.telegramButtons: Telegram buttons need a Telegram channel with "Acknowledge" buttons turned on.
hint.assistantAudit: Needs the Audit log feature (every question is audited).

hint.needsChatAck: Needs Chat acknowledge (account linking and the Telegram poller).
hint.configExcerpts: Also needs "Send configuration excerpts" (Data sharing) and masked configurations.

unknownSources.intro: Senders that are not a monitored device (by host or additional source address). Assign them to a device or ignore them.
unknownSources.assignHint: The address is added to the device's additional source addresses; new records are attributed to it.
unknownSources.ignored: Source added to the ignore list.

eventRules.textHint: Contained in the message (case-insensitive); empty = any.
eventRules.trapOidsHint: One prefix per line; empty = any trap.
eventRules.portsHint: Important: uplinks, LAGs and ports with an interface sensor.

actionHint.warning: Raises a warning condition on the device's event sensor.
actionHint.down: Raises a down condition on the device's event sensor.
actionHint.ignore: Matching messages stop here; later rules are not evaluated.
actionHint.config_backup: Queues a configuration backup of the device (needs Configuration backup on); raises no alert.

eventRules.keyVarbindHint: Tracks instances separately (e.g. ifIndex: port 5 and port 7).
eventRules.keyRegexHint: Exactly one capture group, e.g. interface (\S+)
eventRules.clearingHint: A condition must be able to end: clear on a matching message and/or automatically.
eventRules.clearOnMatch: Clear on a matching message (same key)
eventRules.testHint: Run the rule against the stored records of the last 24 h (no side effects)
